Ashaeiynn: The Sia Tattva Retr eat — Bandh Locks, the Astral Cave, and Mata Shakti Darshan

This transcript is a live, guided multi-day r etreat r ecor ding, made up of several consecutive pieces with no fr esh "welcome" framing between them, all belonging to the same in-person pr ogram (r eferred to at differ ent points as the "bandh sadhna" and the "Sia T attva sadhna"). It opens with a fr esh framing line ("today we ar e going to raise this ener gy upwar d — listen car efully") intr oducing day thr ee of the r etreat's bandh-locking practice, which distinguishes the r etreat as a whole fr om the immediately pr eceding session (Session 1 15's teaching on the physical body and astral rules), so it is tr eated as its own, separate session. The pieces that follow (the astral-cave/Mata Shakti viewing practice, a second day of the water -and-chakra ritual, and a further Mata Shakti darshan with closing Q&A) each continue dir ectly with no fr esh opening, and internal cr oss-r eferences (a participant's question about "after this locking," and the guide's own "like we did yester day") confirm they ar e further days/activities of this same r etreat, so they ar e merged into this one session as Parts F , G, and H. A final piece — the guide's own first-person testimony about a personal astral-world encounter , followed by that night's closing practice instructions (eating times, tilak, sleeping arrangements) matching this r etreat's established logistics — confirms it is a further evening of the same r etreat, so it is mer ged in as Part I. This document describes, in the thir d person, what devotees wer e guided thr ough in these specific live sessions — it is a documentary r ecor d of guided practices that this teaching says r equir e ener gy and pr otection transmitted thr ough the guru's grace, not a self-contained how-to guide for a r eader to perform unsupervised. Part I in particular includes a disturbing first-person account involving a grieving family and a deceased child, pr esented her e strictly as the guide's own cautionary testimony about the risks of unauthorized tantrik practice — never as instruction, and never as something to be r ead literally as medical or psychological guidance for anyone describing similar visions or distr ess. Several parts include explicit warnings fr om the teacher himself that undertaking this kind of practice without a guru's guidance can cause r eal harm, and cautions about how and when it is appr opriate to make personal r equests during these practices. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for the handling rules that govern this material.
Part A — Purpose and Context of the Day's Practice

1. Stated purpose of the session: Per this teaching, the day's practice is directed at raising a devotee's inner ener gy upward, continuing a multi-day series; this session is presented as sealing the third of three "bandhs" (locks) on the body , following two locks described as already sealed on the two preceding days of the series.

2. Traditional yogic framing invoked by this teaching: This teaching links the practice to bandhas referenced in the Patanjali Yoga Sutras (describing mula bandh and other locks), and claims that traditionally sealing all three locks independently — through techniques such as nauli kriya and sustained personal practice — is said to take six to eight months or longer , with many practitioners never fully achieving it despite dedicating years to it.

3. This teaching's claim about how these locks ar e being sealed her e instead: Per this teaching, rather than through months of solitary technique, the three locks are described as being sealed in three days through "sookshm jagat" (subtle-world) shakti
made available through the guru's grace and the grace of awakened saints, working through the specific guided ritual described in Part B.

4. "The physical world is only a manifestation of the astral world," per this teaching: This teaching states that once a lock is sealed in the subtle/astral realm, it is said to manifest in the physical body without delay — illustrated with the suggestion that a yoga teacher checking a devotee's body afterward could confirm the locks are physically present.

5. A broader claim about futur e teaching, per this teaching: The speaker states that Ashaeiynn will continue to open practices of this kind going forward — described as practices that would otherwise take other practitioners six months to ten years of independent ef fort to attain.
Part B — The Guided Ritual, as Described in This Session

This section documents, as a thir d-person r ecor d, the sequence devotees wer e guided thr ough in this specific live session. It is pr esented her e as a description of what happened in this r ecor ding, not as a standalone instructional guide — this teaching frames the practice as dependent on shakti transmitted thr ough the guru, not on the mechanical steps alone.
1. Preparation: Devotees were guided to take a vessel of water and mentally dedicate/of fer it to the guru, treating the guru as witness (sakshi bhaav), before beginning.

2. Breath and lock sequence: Devotees were guided to take a long, deep breath and release it fully , becoming "completely empty ," and then to apply a bandh (lock) by contracting and drawing the anal region upward — described as similar to ashwini mudra.

3. Mantra count while holding: While holding this lock, devotees were guided to mentally repeat "Jai Siyaram" 21 times if possible, or 1 1 times if 21 was not manageable; the teacher stated that either count would allow the lock to complete, though 21 was described as the fuller version.

4. Release and transfer into the water: After the mantra count, devotees were guided to release the body , take another full deep breath, and then direct/breathe that ener gy into the vessel of water .
5. Repetition: This full cycle (breath, lock, mantra, release, breath into water) was directed to be repeated 64 times over the course of the practice.

6. Closing placement: After completing the 64 repetitions, devotees were guided to lift the vessel, place a hand over it, and hold it at the throat chakra (a point of momentary confusion in the live session was clarified as the throat chakra, not the third-eye point) for a minimum of three minutes, with longer being acceptable.

7. Drinking the water: Devotees were instructed that the water in the vessel should ultimately be drunk (not discarded), since per this teaching the water carries the directed ener gy from the practice.

8. Guidance for fatigue during the practice: Per this teaching, a devotee who becomes tired partway through is permitted to take a short (about one-minute) break and then resume the same sequence (lock, mantra, release, breath), continuing until the full 64 repetitions are complete; the speaker acknowledged this is a demanding practice for many participants.

9. Described outcome of completing the practice: Per this teaching, once a devotee completes all 64 repetitions, the three locks are described as becoming fully sealed ("system lock") on the body , described hyperbolically as holding regardless of whether the devotee is able to eat.
Part C — Cautions Attached to the Practice

1. A caution against discussing the practice or one's own attainment with others: Per this teaching, a devotee should not create any "loophole" by revealing their progress or the fact that these locks have been sealed to other people; per this teaching, doing so is described as causing the locks to reopen immediately , at which point the held ener gy would flow back downward and the ef fect would be lost.
2. Locks ar e also described as r eopening if a devotee "violates the rules" — this teaching does not specify further what this means beyond general practice discipline.

3. Framing for how a devotee should describe this practice if asked, per this teaching: Rather than claiming personal credit ("I sealed a lock"), a devotee is instructed to attribute it to the guru ("our guru sealed it"), consistent with this teaching's broader emphasis on guru-grace over individual achievement.
Part D — On Using Every Available Spiritual Tool

1. This teaching's stance on scriptural authority: Per this teaching, while the Patanjali Yoga Sutras are described as highly authoritative, the speaker cautions that "not everything is only that" and "not everything else is untrue either" — framing all traditional tools and techniques (yogic and otherwise) as things a devotee should learn to use, rather than relying on a single system exclusively .
Part E — Clarifications Exchanged Live During the Practice

1. Where to hold the water: In response to a participant's question, the teacher clarified that if a devotee cannot hold the water vessel directly in their hand throughout, keeping it resting in a container/plate near them is acceptable, so long as the same water is ultimately drunk afterward rather than poured out.

2. Confirming the point of placement: In response to live confusion during the session, the teacher confirmed the vessel should be placed at the throat chakra at the end of the sequence, not the third-eye point.
3. A brief resolve (sankalp) was taken at the start of the session , with the practice noted as being recorded, consistent with this project's other guided-practice sessions.
Part F — The Astral Cave and Mata Shakti Viewing Practice

This section documents a further guided practice fr om the same r etreat, held on a later day . A participant's own question during the session ("is this mor e visible after this locking/chakravan?") confirms it follows the bandh-locking practice described in Parts A–C.

1. Origin claim tied to this practice: Per this teaching, Hanuman ji Maharaj became the giver of the eight siddhis and nine nidhis by learning these very vidyas (mystical sciences) from Mata (the divine mother), who had promised to teach and grant them to him; this is described as having occurred at what this teaching calls the most "mystic" — and, in the same breath, most "fearsome" — site in the Vedic tradition, the same site referenced for this practice.

2. A caution given befor e the exer cise began: The guide told participants to stay close together during the exercise, explicitly stating he could not guarantee anyone's safety if they became separated or "hit" by something during it.

3. Entering the "cave" (guided visualization): Devotees were guided to imagine entering a cave, with the sensation described as similar to water being poured over them — framed as a purification process in which many of a devotee's subtler bodies are removed, leaving only four main ones.

4. The circling (parikrama): Devotees were guided to mentally circle a domed structure at least 108 times, quickly , through mental prayer/resolve rather than physical movement — described as the subtle body acting automatically once the intention is set.

5. Stated purpose of the cir cling, per this teaching: (a) so devotees can view the coming ener gy in a more controlled state, and (b) because the ener gy itself is described as capable of pulling a devotee in or taking control of them, which this teaching explicitly calls "dangerous" — making the preparatory circling necessary .

6. A collective invocation was led , addressed to Hanuman ji Maharaj, referencing an ener gy described as known only to Mata Sita and, through her , to Bhagwan Ram; the prayer asked to see this element gently , not to be overtaken or controlled by it, and for protection. The guide explicitly stated that reaching this point without a guru's guidance can lead to real harm, and that a person can fall prey to various forces without such guidance.

7. Guidance for what to do if something appears: Devotees were told to bow (pranam) if Mata's glimpse or ener gy appeared; if nothing was visible, to mentally look toward the sky , where the ener gy is described as visible from above; and to respond to any faint sensation or vibration in the body with repeated pranam to the perceived shakti.

8. An explicit caution against making r equests during this specific practice: The guide directly warned devotees not to ask for or demand anything while in this state, stating that doing so would mean "she" would ask something of the devotee in return that they would not be able to give — framed as a serious caution, not an invitation.

9. Devotees' described experiences, documented her e as r eported in the live session: a bluish, transparent ener gy described by several participants as having a strong "pulling"/attracting quality; a goldish "seed" at the center , compared to a Sri Chakra; chest heaviness and vibration, described by the guide as "ener gy exchange" (the devotee's own ener gy going out, the source's ener gy coming in); increasing stability over time for some; and an orange-colored light or flame rising upward for others.

10. This teaching's own explanation of the energy observed: Described as ever -moving and without one fixed color — appearing bluish on the surface but reddish at its "core," changing automatically , likened to flowing water or a wave; this teaching states the ener gy was awakened by Mata and bound, then released downward, at Bhagwan Ram's feet, linked to the Ram Tarak mantra and Mata Sita.

1 1. Closing instruction for the subtle body: Devotees were told to instruct their own subtle body (sookshm sharir) to remain at the site, continuing japa under the guru's presence, never to leave the place and never to break the guru's word — with an explicit warning that stepping outside the guru's protection would cause problems — and to pray for the guru's protection over this connection.

12. Closing of the practice: Devotees were told that of fering pranam to the site's earth and to the guru would bring a sensation of warmth as the ener gy moved downward, at which point they should immediately rub their hands together , place them over their eyes, and slowly open their eyes.
Part G — Sia Tattva Sadhna: A Second Guided Water -and-Chakra Ritual

This section documents a further day of a r elated guided ritual within the same r etreat, r eferred to her e as "Sia T attva sadhna." A participant's r emark ("yester day we placed it at the navel") confirms this is a later day of a multi-day version of the water -vessel practice.

1. Opening r esolve (sankalp): A formal spoken resolve was led collectively , dedicating the day's sadhna ("Sia Tattva jagran," described as the "first chapter") to Hanuman ji Maharaj as guide and witness, invoking the guru's word, method, and teaching, and specifically requesting protection alongside the awakening.

2. Breath, mantra, and water sequence: Devotees were guided to take a long, deep breath and release it fully; then to mentally repeat "Jai Siyaram" 1 1 times; then take another deep breath and direct/breathe it into a vessel of water . This cycle was directed to be repeated 72 times.

3. Grounding after the repetitions: After completing the 72 repetitions, devotees were guided to place both hands flat on the ground and continue mental japa, described as drawing a strong ener gy from "Dharti Mata" (Mother Earth), with this teaching stating that "Mata Sita's tattva" begins reaching the devotee from this point onward.

4. Placement at a chakra point (this day of the series): After the breath-and-water cycle, devotees were guided to lift the water vessel and hold it, with a hand sealing it closed, at the heart chakra for three to four minutes — noted as dif fering from the previous day's placement at the navel.

5. Closing of this day's ritual: After the holding period, devotees set the vessel down, raised both hands, placed them on the ground again, and continued audible (rather than only mental) japa, praying to Bhagwan Ram and Mata Sita to be included in the sadhna and for their own "Sia tattva" to awaken within them; the guide noted the water in the vessel would later be taken/consumed once the day's resolve was declared complete.
Part H — Mata Shakti Darshan: Invocation, Viewing, and Closing Guidance

This section documents a further guided Mata Shakti darshan (viewing) session within the same r etreat, held on a day the guide references as being after Holi, and closing with gr oup Q&A and forwar d-looking guidance.

1. Framing of the darshan: Devotees were told no travel was needed to reach Mata, since Mata is described as self-manifest (swayambhu) right where they were; devotees were guided to invoke her mentally , opening with collective chanting ("Jai Siyaram") and traditional bhajan verses (including lines from the Hanuman Chalisa, "Mangal bhavan amangal hari," and other devotional couplets).

2. Guidance on r ecognizing the appr oach of the energy: Devotees were told that if a reddish tint appears, they should look upward toward the sky; if a rose or pink coloration appears, this indicates Mata's ener gy is beginning to reach them, and they were told that looking toward the sky would let Mata reveal her own element to them.

3. Devotees' described experiences (documented as r eported in the live session): a "bol" (voice/sound)-like sensation described by one participant as simple, with an association to a book and a resolved sense of "hunger" within; visible light for some; a "crowd" impression for one participant that resolved into a full form of Mata described in a red saree, adorned in gold, standing before the group; devotees were guided to bow to this form.

4. An explicit invitation to make personal r equests, distinct from the caution in Part F: Unlike the caution given during the cave-viewing practice, in this darshan devotees were explicitly told they could ask Mata, in their minds, for whatever they wished, after first of fering their sadhna for acceptance and asking for her grace.

5. Closing of the darshan and subtle-body guidance: Devotees were guided to bow at Mata's feet, and then instructed to formally request (through the guru) that all their subtle bodies (sookshm shariras) be safely reunited with their physical bodies; the guide advised that devotees could either leave their subtle body at the guru's feet or bring it back with them, personally recommending leaving it at the guru's feet via a witnessed (sakshi bhaav) request, then closing by rubbing the hands, placing them over the eyes, and slowly opening the eyes.

6. Q&A: why some devotees felt nothing, per this teaching: The guide explained that a lack of any felt experience typically traces to one of three causes — an existing dosha on the person, an unresolved pitru-related resolve, or a subtle body still too underdeveloped for the physical body to register it — and that the remedy in all three cases is the same: continuing regular japa
and sitting in havans, which will gradually clear the barrier; devotees were reassured that benefit "will" come with consistent practice, and told not to worry .

7. The guide's own stated pr eference about visible experience: The guide stated he personally considers it better for most devotees not to have vivid personal visions early on, since visible experience can make people arrogant; he described himself as capable of seeing on their behalf where needed.

8. Closing acknowledgment and blessing: The guide stated that the "Sia tattva sadhna" (first chapter) was complete for the group, with a guru-gaddi blessing extended to all, and separately of fered his own recommendation/prayer that those who completed 70% or more of the practice have their sadhna accepted — explicitly framed as his own recommendation to the guru, not a guarantee, alongside a general prayer for devotees' guidance, knowledge, and protection.

9. A closing caution about doubting the guru's own guide: The guide addressed devotees who privately doubt whether his own stated guide (Hanuman ji Maharaj) is real or just something he says, listing several reasons devotees should trust the claim (consistency over time, not repeating it needlessly , encouraging daily practice rather than assuming it), and connected restlessness in a devotee's life to for getting their own guru.

10. Forward-looking guidance: Devotees were told to continue normal japa for a day or two, informed that Hanuman Jayanti was approaching and would involve further preparation, and given permission to resume normal eating (with a specific note that a stricter fasting resolve could be broken after midnight or after 3 a.m. for anyone who needed to eat sooner).
Part I — The Guide's Own Testimony: A Failed Rescue in the Astral World

This section documents a further evening of the same r etreat, in which the guide shar es a first-person account of a personal astralworld encounter befor e assigning that night's practice. It is r ecor ded her e strictly as the guide's own cautionary testimony — never as instruction, and never as literal medical or psychological guidance for a r eader who describes similar experiences.

1. Context for the account: The guide explained that he sometimes practices sadhna alone rather than with the group; on the occasion described here, he had grown exhausted during solitary practice and fell asleep in his seated posture.
2. The summons: While asleep, he describes being woken by a kick from a "soul"/spirit who told him it was time to go; he initially feared this meant his own death, but was told he would go alone.

3. Arrival at a gate: Closing his eyes, he found himself before two old, world-weary gatekeeper -like figures (described as casually smoking, apparently unconcerned) who asked what he "had" that qualified him to be sent through; he answered that he had nothing of his own except his guru's grace. This answer , though it did not fully satisfy them, was accepted, and he was let through.

4. The house in South India: He was led to a home where a grieving family — a husband, his wife, the husband's younger brother , and two children (one an infant) — was in visible distress and begged him for help; he reassured them, framing the visit as routine work assigned by his guru ("Baba").

5. What he found: In the bedroom, part of the wall had been transformed into what he describes as a literal doorway into the astral world — blue-colored, with water appearing to flow upward across a blue "ceiling" — which he identifies as the result of prior ritual work, including what the family described as sacrifices ("baliyan"), performed by the two brothers in an attempt to open contact with the subtle world.

6. What the doorway connected to: He states it had been linked to a specific, distressing realm of deceased children that he describes having visited "the day before"; the woman of the house was, at that moment, holding a dead infant connected to that realm, crying and pleading for the connection to be severed.

7. His own r eaction: He describes this as the first time he ever felt genuine fear in an encounter of this kind, distinguishing it from the routine hauntings/disturbances he had grown used to — the visible anguish of the mother specifically overwhelmed him.

8. What happened next: He found his own ener gy draining in that realm and felt unable to act; overwhelmed, he left without resolving the situation, and describes this candidly as a personal failure — reflecting that he may not yet have been suf ficiently prepared for what his guru had sent him to address.

9. How he says he r esponded to this failur e: Rather than treating it as defeat, he describes committing to study further and attempt the same case again, framing the episode as a lesson in humility — noting that many unseen circumstances are quietly waiting for a devotee's own readiness. He also noted that the two brothers, despite their family's suf fering and their own visibly deteriorated health (described as blackened teeth and poor condition), denied any wrongdoing, insisting they had only performed sadhna.

10. A related case cited as pr ecedent: The guide separately mentions being one of only three people worldwide reportedly appointed by devtas to dismantle a specific tantrik's network, describing that particular ef fort as fully successful within about a year and a half — of fered as evidence that this kind of work can succeed, even though the case described above ended in retreat rather than resolution.

1 1. His closing caution to devotees: Not to place excessive trust in what is visible to the ordinary physical eye, framing the subtle/astral world as preceding and shaping what later appears in the physical world.

12. That night's closing practice instructions: Devotees were told to perform tilak for their photo/image of "Baba," of fer rice, flowers, and tilak as personally appropriate, and pray to be included in the guru lineage; told not to eat after 6 p.m. but permitted to drink water , and that they could eat again after 3 a.m. or after sunrise; and told they could sleep on the ground rather than requiring a raised bed for that night's practice.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session r ecords a specific guided gr oup practice (a thr ee-day "triple bandh" sequence) as a documentary account of what devotees were guided through in this recording — not as a standalone instructional guide for unsupervised practice. This teaching frames the result as dependent on shakti transmitted through the guru's grace, not on mechanically repeating the steps alone. The practice as described combines a br eath-hold, an anal-r egion lock (similar to ashwini mudra), a 21-count (or 1 1count) mantra r epetition, and dir ecting br eath/energy into a vessel of water , repeated 64 times , followed by holding the vessel at the throat chakra for at least three minutes and later drinking the water . This teaching links the practice to bandhas described in the Patanjali Yoga Sutras , claiming that what traditionally takes six to eight months (or longer) of independent yogic practice is here conferred in three days through guru-transmitted shakti — presented as this teaching's own claim, not independently verified. Devotees ar e cautioned not to discuss their own attainment of these locks with others , per this teaching, since doing so is described as causing the locks to reopen; credit for the result is to be attributed to the guru's grace, not personal achievement. Fatigue during the practice is accommodated with short br eaks , rather than stopping — the speaker acknowledges this is demanding. This teaching frames all traditional spiritual tools and techniques as available for a devotee to learn , rather than treating any single scriptural system as the sole authority . A later guided practice (the astral-cave/Mata Shakti viewing) is documented her e as a gr oup visualization exer cise carrying the teacher's own explicit warning that it is not safe to attempt without a guru's guidance , and an explicit

caution against making requests/demands of the perceived ener gy during that specific exercise, since this teaching describes the ener gy as capable of exerting pull/control over the practitioner . A separate, r elated ritual r eferred to as "Sia Tattva sadhna" combines a br eath/mantra/water sequence (72 r epetitions) with holding the water vessel at a chakra point (navel one day , heart chakra the next) and gr ounding hands on the floor , documented here as this teaching's own multi-day retreat practice, not a standalone how-to. A further Mata Shakti darshan (viewing) session, unlike the cave-viewing exer cise, explicitly permits devotees to mentally make personal r equests of Mata — this document notes this contrast rather than resolving it, since both are recorded exactly as this teaching presents them. Devotees who r eported no felt experience wer e told this typically traces to an existing dosha, an unr esolved pitru-r elated resolve, or an underdeveloped subtle body — with consistent japa and havan attendance as the stated r emedy in all cases , not a personal failing. The guide's own first-person testimony (Part I) describes a failed attempt to help a grieving family entangled with a deceased child thr ough an impr operly-opened astral "doorway" — recorded strictly as his own cautionary , devotional account of the risks of unauthorized tantrik practice and the limits of his own readiness, never as instruction for opening such a connection, and never as literal guidance for anyone describing similar visions or grief. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Part A–E: The Bandh Sadhna (Br eath-Lock Practice)

Q1. What was the stated purpose of this day's practice? A1. Per this teaching, to raise a devotee's inner ener gy upward, sealing the third of three "bandhs" (ener gy locks) on the body — the first two described as sealed on the two preceding days of the retreat.

Q2. How does this teaching r elate the practice to traditional yoga? A2. It links the three locks to bandhas described in the Patanjali Yoga Sutras, claiming that independently sealing all three traditionally takes six to eight months or longer of dedicated practice (via techniques like nauli kriya), with many practitioners never fully achieving it.

Q3. How does this teaching say the locks ar e being sealed her e instead? A3. Per this teaching, through subtle-world (sookshm jagat) shakti made available by the guru's grace and the grace of awakened saints, via the specific guided ritual — not through months of solitary technique.

Q4. What does "the physical world is only a manifestation of the astral world" mean her e? A4. This teaching claims that once a lock is sealed in the subtle/astral realm, it manifests in the physical body without delay — illustrated with the suggestion that a yoga teacher could confirm the locks physically afterward.

Q5. What did the guided ritual involve, as documented in this r ecording? A5. Devotees dedicated a vessel of water to the guru, took a long breath and released it fully , applied an anal-region lock (similar to ashwini mudra) while mentally repeating "Jai Siyaram" 21 (or 1 1) times, then released, took another breath, and directed that breath/ener gy into the water — repeated 64 times, followed by holding the vessel at the throat chakra for at least three minutes and later drinking the water .

Q6. What if a devotee got tir ed partway thr ough? A6. They were permitted a short (about one-minute) break before resuming the same sequence; the guide acknowledged this is demanding for many participants.

Q7. What caution did the guide give about discussing this practice with others? A7. Per this teaching, revealing one's own progress or attainment of these locks to others is described as causing the locks to reopen immediately , undoing the ef fect — devotees were told to credit the guru's grace rather than claim personal achievement if asked.

Q8. What did the guide say about scriptural authority? A8. That while the Patanjali Yoga Sutras are highly authoritative, "not everything is only that, and not everything else is untrue either" — framing all traditional tools as things a devotee should learn to use rather than relying on one system exclusively .

Q9. What practical clarifications wer e given live during the practice? A9. That the water vessel can rest nearby rather than being held in-hand throughout (so long as the water is later drunk, not discarded), and that the vessel should be held at the throat chakra, not the third-eye point, at the end of the sequence.
Part F: The Astral Cave and Mata Shakti Viewing Practice

Q10. What origin story is tied to this practice? A10. Q12. What did the guided "cave" visualization involve? A12. Devotees imagined entering a cave with a sensation like water being poured over them, described as a purification process removing many of a devotee's subtler bodies and leaving only four main ones; they then mentally circled a domed structure at least 108 times through prayer/resolve rather than physical movement.

Q13. Why was the cir cling done, per this teaching? A13. To let devotees view the coming ener gy in a more controlled state, and because the ener gy itself is described as capable of pulling a devotee in or exerting control over them — explicitly called "dangerous" by the teacher .

Q14. What warning did the guide give about attempting this without a guru? A14.
